hook.text: What is Pomerol's crasse de fer?
hook.answer: iron oxides in the subsoil ('sous-sol comportant des oxydes de fer ou « crasse de fer »')
hook.source: INAO cahier des charges AOC Pomerol (decree 2011-1613, mod. 2014-904; 2021 PNO file), X.1

station.name: St Emilion
station.period: sheet 1991-2020, but temperature and precipitation 1995-2020, sunshine 2006-2020 (footnote)

station_note: Values reused from facts/deep-saint-emilion.json (official Météo-France fiche read on 2026-11-11). Station at 44.9175 N, -0.1878 E, about 2 km from the Pomerol outline centre, at the Pomerol / Saint-Émilion edge.

precip_year_mm.how: sum of monthly precip St Emilion 1995-2020 (fiche total 798.1)

claims.claim: Area: commune of Pomerol plus part of Libourne (1928 judgment), north limit the Barbanne

claims.source: Open Wine Atlas Study, Right Bank lesson

claims.claim: 3.2 km from Libourne; Dordogne 3.4 km; Bordeaux 31 km
claims.source: Open Wine Atlas near_town, rivers, near_city

claims.claim: Ground 8 to 40 m, mean 24 m; 85% flat
claims.source: Open Wine Atlas terrain e=[8,24,40,15,36], flat 0.85

claims.claim: Relatively flat relief sloping towards the Isle valley; Günz terrace 30 to 40 m, Riss terraces 20 to 25 m
Soils: gravels, sands, reddened pebbles, smectite-rich Tertiary clays; subsoil with iron oxides (crasse de fer)

claims.source: Open Wine Atlas Study, Right Bank lesson

claims.claim: 5 varieties allowed: Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cot (Malbec), Merlot, Petit Verdot; no proportion rules
